 Syrian, Jordanian chiefs meet to tackle border smuggling issues
 Maj. Gen. Ali al-Naasan, Syria’s General Staff Chief meets with a delegation from Jordan, Nov. 15, 2026 (SANA) Short Url https://arab.news/p4t96
 Updated 16 November 2026 09:35 Arab News November 16, 2026 09:35 Follow The meeting in Damascus included several Syrian and Jordanian officers, focusing on enhancing security cooperation
 Both countries face regional threats from criminal drug gangs and the security risks posed by the Daesh group
 Updated 16 November 2026 09:35 Arab News November 16, 2026 09:35 Follow LONDON: Chief of General Staff in the Syrian Arab Republic Maj. Gen. Ali al-Naasan met with Brig. Gen. Nael Mohammad Abdullah, Jordanian commander of the Strategic Planning Team, to discuss border control and efforts to combat smuggling.
 Several Syrian and Jordanian officers attended the meeting in Damascus on Sunday to discuss common interests and strengthen security cooperation between the two countries, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency.
 In April, the Syrian Ministry of Interior intercepted a major attempt to smuggle 943 kilograms of captagon through the Jaber border crossing into Jordan. Both countries are confronted with various regional threats, including criminal drug gangs and the security threat posed by the Daesh group.
